claims.claim: First Solar links thin-film module manufacturing capacity to utility-scale generation buildout and electricity supply, serving the human need for reliable scalable power; its large contracted backlog indicates demand visibility but observed terminations prove that backlog is conditional rather than guaranteed.

Scenario robustness depends on module cost/performance, manufacturing execution, policy/trade conditions, grid/permitting and customer project economics; grid/interconnection and project finance can become successor bottlenecks even when module supply is available.

causalEdges: utility-scale electricity demand -> solar project buildout -> module demand -> First Solar manufacturing -> generation capacity
customer project economics/policy/permitting -> contract durability -> backlog realization
module availability -> grid/interconnection/project finance as successor bottlenecks

risks.risk: Contract termination evidence means backlog cannot be treated as equivalent to realized revenue.

contradictions.contradiction: Large backlog and reaffirmed guidance coexist with revenue pressure from customer terminations; this narrows confidence in backlog quality without invalidating current execution.

unknowns.unknown: Cancellation-adjusted backlog economics and policy/tariff sensitivity are not quantified in the reused evidence.

claims.claim: Observed customer terminations are a concrete red-team check against backlog/TAM confidence inflation; the correct improvement path is to distinguish contracted volume from cancellation-adjusted economic value.

Substitution pressure includes competing crystalline-silicon modules and other generation technologies; a falsifier of durable differentiation would be sustained pricing/margin deterioration or cancellations attributable to inferior delivered economics rather than isolated customer events.

risks.risk: Policy, permitting, financing and customer project economics can reduce backlog conversion independently of manufacturing execution.
Backlog volume can overstate resilience if termination rights or economic adjustments are material.

contradictions.contradiction: Current profitability and guidance support execution while terminations demonstrate non-zero demand fragility; both facts should remain represented.

unknowns.unknown: The present evidence does not quantify cancellation rights, tariff sensitivity or cancellation-adjusted backlog margin.
